summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for severe bilateral leg cramps and hyperglycemia with glucose up to 500. Labs revealed hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and acute-on-chronic kidney injury likely due to dehydration and uncontrolled diabetes exacerbated by prednisone. She was treated with IV fluids and albumin, which resolved her electrolyte abnormalities and myalgias. A diagnostic paracentesis showed mild ascites without infection. Her insulin regimen was optimized with a switch to 70/30 NPH-humalog 40 units in the morning and 20 units at bedtime, along with a sliding scale. She was instructed to report daily blood glucose values to her diabetologist. Her condition stabilized, and she was discharged home with follow-up arranged.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease with stage 1 through stage 4 chronic kidney disease, or unspecified chronic kidney disease
Adverse effect of glucocorticoids and synthetic analogues, initial encounter
